analysis.title: Carlisle Companies Inc. (CSL) 3Q26 Recap: Steady Re-Roof Activity, Cost Actions, and Price Realization Continue, Allowing for Upside to Margins Over Time
key_insights: Carlisle reported 3Q26 adj. EPS of $5.92 vs GS estimate $5.90 and FactSet consensus $5.89. Revenue rose 8.6% vs GSe +4.8%, adding $0.21 to EPS, partly offset by an adj. EBIT margin of 20.5%, 63bps below the GS model, which cost $0.18.

CCM revenue rose 8.4% YOY vs GSe +5.4% on re-roof demand, pricing and strategic initiatives. Segment EBITDA margin fell 200bps YOY to 28.2% vs GSe 29.0% as negative price/cost outweighed productivity and operating leverage.

CWT organic sales grew 9.4% YOY vs GSe +3.1%, driven by share gains and weather-related demand for roof coatings, despite weak new construction. Segment EBITDA margin rose 60bps YOY to 18.0% vs GSe 19.8%.

GS sees potential for upward revisions to sales and margins as conditions stabilize, citing new product momentum, cost actions (management cited 500bps of expansion in CWT masked by record diesel prices) and re-roof activity that GS views as fairly resilient to the macro.

Re-roof demand in CCM was up mid-single digits, offsetting a similar decline in new construction. Channel inventories have normalized after a modest 2Q pull-forward, with strength holding into October. GS expects low-single-digit volume growth in 4Q.
GS models 4Q CCM sales +8.7% YOY and +6.7% in 2027, CWT 4Q sales +7.9% and +3.7% in 2027, and consolidated 4Q growth of 8.5% with full-year +5.8% and 2027 +5.9%.
Management said 9 of 12 new products have launched this year, with the rest on track. The company targets 25% of total sales from products introduced in the last 5 years.

Rising diesel and freight costs pushed price/cost parity out one quarter. 2027 is expected to be price/cost positive if energy and freight hold at current levels. Price realization was +4% in CCM and +3% in CWT in 3Q, with a +7% CCM guide for 4Q.

Costs rose double digits in 2Q, high-teens in 3Q, and are expected to rise mid-to-high teens in 4Q. Carlisle took three price increases in CCM and two in CWT this year, including one in October, plus freight surcharges.

GS looks for relief in MDI and polyols as force majeures lift. It models low-single-digit price increases in each segment in 2027, with price/cost tailwinds peaking in 2Q before easing on tougher comps.
GS forecasts 4Q adj. EBITDA margin of 26.8% in CCM (flat YOY) and 16.8% in CWT (+95bps YOY). For 2027 it models +92bps in CCM and +146bps in CWT. GS calls current margin headwinds transitory.

Net debt/EBITDA was 1.8x at 3Q end, vs 1.4x a year ago, with $547mn of cash. 3Q FCF from continuing operations was $277mn. Capex is on track for $180mn this year, down from $200mn. Management repurchased $350mn of stock in the quarter, and the full-year buyback guide holds at $1.2bn.

GS models FCF of $802mn this year (~15.1% of sales, consistent with guidance) and $909mn in 2027. Management sees bolt-on M&A opportunities in building envelope while staying disciplined on valuation.

GS raised its 2026 adj. EPS estimate to $21.05 from $21.10 (a cut), its 2027 estimate to $24.70 from $24.45, and its 2028 estimate to $29.15 from $28.30. The 12-month price target moves to $480 from $464, based on 14.5x (vs 15.0x) Q5-Q8 adj. EBITDA. Rating stays Buy (Conviction List).
Scenario analysis: upside case $524 (19.4x 2027 EPS), downside case $291 (13.1x 2027 EPS). GS sees favorable risk/reward at $345.21.

market_movers.rationale: PT raised to $480 from $464 on 14.5x Q5-Q8 adj. EBITDA (down from 15.0x). GS sees upside to margins over time from cost actions, price realization and new products, with 39.0% upside to the target.

sector_views.rationale: GS rates CSL Buy, expecting steady re-roof activity, price realization and cost actions to support margins even with a soft macro and weak new construction.

earnings_insights: CSL 3Q26 adj. EPS reported $5.92 vs GS estimate $5.90 and FactSet consensus $5.89. Revenue grew 8.6% YOY vs GSe +4.8%. Adj. EBIT margin was 20.5%, 63bps below GS's model.
GS full-year estimates (adj. EPS, forecasts): 2026E $21.05 (from $21.10), 2027E $24.70 (from $24.45), 2028E $29.15 (from $28.30). Next-quarter EPS estimates: 4Q26E $4.47, 1Q27E $4.23, 2Q27E $8.61.
GS 4Q26 forecasts: consolidated sales growth of 8.5%, CCM adj. EBITDA margin 26.8% (flat YOY), CWT 16.8% (+95bps YOY). GS believes the company's 4Q guide and 2027 estimates could be conservative.

macro_indicators.reading: Record high diesel prices in 3Q; Carlisle input costs up high-teens in 3Q and expected up mid-to-high teens in 4Q
macro_indicators.interpretation: Input cost inflation pushed price/cost parity out one quarter. A decline in energy prices would create price/cost tailwinds for CSL.

macro_indicators.reading: Weak new construction; CWT noted a mid-single digit decline in housing, CCM new construction down mid-single digits
macro_indicators.interpretation: Re-roof activity has offset the new-construction decline, so GS sees CSL's volumes as fairly resilient to the housing macro.

trade_ideas.rationale: Cost actions, price realization and new products should support margin upside over time, with a favorable risk/reward skew.
trade_ideas.risk: Raw material cost increases that cannot be passed through, execution on strategic initiatives and acquisitions, productivity shortfalls, loss of key customer orders, and new competition.

risk_factors: An increase in raw material costs and the inability to pass them through
Failure to execute on key strategic initiatives, including closing and integrating announced acquisitions
Productivity and efficiency efforts that do not meet expectations
Loss or change in order patterns from key customers
Increased competition if newer entrants seek to gain share
Limited visibility on energy prices and the path for price/cost

tension_points.bull_case: Cost actions (CWT largely complete), price realization, new products and easing energy and MDI/polyol costs should produce price/cost tailwinds and margin upside over time. GS sees the 4Q guide and 2027 estimates as potentially conservative.
tension_points.bear_case: 3Q margins missed expectations as negative price/cost outweighed productivity. Diesel, freight and input costs rose high-teens and are expected up mid-to-high teens in 4Q, pushing price/cost parity out one quarter. GS cut its target multiple to 14.5x on limited visibility.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Raw material and energy costs keep rising and cannot be passed through, so price/cost does not turn positive in 2027 as management expects.

theme_stances.key_argument: Price realization and cost actions should turn price/cost positive in 2027 if energy and freight hold, giving margin upside.
theme_stances.evidence: we believe the current margin headwinds are transitory

theme_stances.evidence: steady re-roof activity that we believe is fairly resilient to the macro
